newsitem.title: USA: U.S. opens record Gulf of Mexico lease sale round.
newsitem.headline: U.S. opens record Gulf of Mexico lease sale round.

text.p: Racing to snatch up new deepwater drilling sites, oil and natural gas producers have submitted a record number of bids in the latest lease round in the Gulf of Mexico, results of which are due later Thursday.
Shattering last year's record lease round, producers bid on 1,790 tracts in federal waters off the coast of Louisiana, the U.S. Minerals Management Service said on Wednesday.

"This continues a trend from last year," agency spokesman Barney Congdon said, referring to an April 1996 sale that drew 1,381 bids and itself smashed a 16-year record for the activity in a single lease round.

In the annual lease sales, producers submit sealed bids on rights to drill in a specified tract in the Gulf. Additional payments, known as royalties, are also paid on oil and gas lifted from the leaseholdings.
A lower royalty rate on deepwater tracts sparked active bidding in waters 800 metres (2,625 feet) or deeper, with producers bidding on 587 tracts eligible for royalty relief.

The active bidding was credited with pushing offshore drilling stocks up sharply on Tuesday. A tight supply of available offshore drilling rigs was seen boosting dayrates of the offshore services firms.
"We thought it would be a strong lease sale," said Dave Herasimchuk, vice president of market development for Global Marine Inc in Houston.
Played out in a downtown New Orleans hotel, the annual gatherings are a barometer of drilling activity in the Gulf and the health of the domestic industry.
This year, bids were expected to soar from oil companies flush with cash after posting record profits from last year's strong oil and gas prices.

"If we see a lot of shelf play, then you've got to think this is fueled by higher demand," said Blake Wright, an offshore analyst with Offshore Data Services. "I'm really going to need to see where the bids are going to fall, where the water depths are going to be."
The majors were expected to again dominate bidding on deepwater tracts, led by Shell Offshore Inc, Chevron Corp, Texaco Inc, Conoco Inc, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co and Amoco Corp.
Producers Norcen Energy Resources Ltd and Elf Exploration also have locked in long-term contracts on offshore drilling rigs, and were expected to emerge as active bidders, Wright said.

Although deepwater tracts were the prime attraction, producers have not ignored the safer plays in the shallower waters of the shelf. Bids were submitted on 445 tracts in waters less than 400 metres (1,312 feet) deep, according to the MMS, which regulates oil and gas production offshore.
